paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: following Jesus doesn't always feel easy, and some of His words are hard to take. Many of His disciples said, "This is a difficult teaching. Who can accept it?" (John 6:60). Then many of them "turned back and no longer walked with Him" (John 6:66). That's the moment to ask yourself whether His words are worth more to you than being comfortable.

Now look at what Jesus asks the Twelve: "Do you want to leave too?" (John 6:67). Peter answers, "Lord, to whom would we go? You have the words of eternal life." (John 6:68). He doesn't say he understands every bit of it. He says there's nowhere else worth going, and I'll tell you, friend, that's an answer you can stand on even when your head is still spinning.

So when a teaching in the Word stretches you, don't walk off. Stay at the table and keep asking, the way Peter stayed. This passage also shows that being near Jesus and truly believing are not the same thing, because John tells us Judas was one of the Twelve and still "was later to betray Jesus" (John 6:71). I'm proud of you for showing up to the oven, baker, so keep coming back to the words that give life.
